\chapter{Introduction}

Farmers water too much when they cannot see how wet the soil is. Commercial
probes give good readings but cost more than a small farm will spend. This
report tests whether capacitive sensors that cost a few euros each are good
enough to decide when to water.

\begin{remark}
All measurements were taken in one field over one season; the results may not
carry over to clay soils.
\end{remark}

The rest of the report describes the hardware in Chapter~\ref{ch:hardware}
and the measurements in Chapter~\ref{ch:results}.
